findings.title: WhatsApp sends bypass the retry/queue/dead-letter machinery — a transient outage destroys the message
findings.scenario: A Meta Cloud API 5xx / network blip during a business-initiated template (or interactive, or carousel) send. _deliver_whatsapp/send_interactive/send_carousel record status 'failed' DIRECTLY and never call _on_failure(), so with NOTIFY_DELIVERY_MODE=queued (the default) the message is NOT queued, NOT retried, and NOT dead-lettered — it is silently lost, exactly the 'a five-minute outage destroys every message' bug the retry system was built to prevent. Email/SMS get the queue+retry treatment; the platform's flagship channel does not.
findings.evidence: return await rec(recipient, "whatsapp", template_key, "failed", provider=provider, error="send failed")
findings.recommendation: Route WhatsApp send failures through the same _on_failure()/RetryPolicy path as email/SMS (classify retryable vs permanent, queue with backoff), and make drain() re-send WhatsApp deliveries via the delivery's OWN tenant/number rather than the default pool.
findings.fix: WhatsApp TEMPLATE send failures now route through _on_failure (classify/queue/backoff) like email/SMS instead of recording 'failed' and being destroyed; drain() re-sends queued WhatsApp deliveries via a new _wa_resend from the stored payload. A per-branch whatsapp_override send stays 'failed' (a queued retry would send from the wrong number). Pre-send validation failures remain permanent. Regression tests: outage→queued→drain→sent, and override-not-queued.

findings.title: notify() failure paths bypass _finish(), leaking the idempotency reservation
findings.scenario: A caller sends with an idempotency_key on an email/SMS whose template is missing or whose render throws. These two branches return _record(...) directly instead of _finish(idempotency_key, ...). The reservation placed by _dedupe_reserve() (result=None) is therefore never released. A legitimate retry within NOTIFY_DEDUPE_TTL_SECONDS (default 24h) — even after the template is fixed — hits idempotent_get() (returns None because result is None), then reserve_idempotent() (cas fails, slot exists, not expired), and is handed a bogus {"duplicate": true, "in_progress": true} for up to 24h, never sending.
findings.evidence:
if tmpl is None:
            return await self._record(recipient, channel, template_key, "failed", tenant=tenant or "", error="template not found")
findings.recommendation: Wrap both early-return failure branches in _finish(idempotency_key, tenant or "", await self._record(...)) so a non-remembered outcome releases the reservation, matching the unknown-channel branch above them.
findings.fix: the missing-template and render-failure early returns in notify() now go through _finish() so the idempotency reservation is released on a non-remembered failure, matching the other branches — a legitimate retry is no longer deduped as in_progress until the TTL.

findings.title: Native-pay refund (money movement) is neither audited nor idempotent
findings.scenario: POST /internal/whatsapp/pay/refund moves money via Meta but writes NO audit record (unlike every other privileged action in the service, e.g. whatsapp.test_send, secret_set) and accepts no idempotency_key. A redelivered/duplicated internal call, or an investigation into 'who refunded this order', has no witness. The only defense is the lookup 'captured' state check, which is a two-call TOCTOU (see notification-004), not a durable audit.
findings.evidence:
@router.post("/refund", dependencies=[Depends(require_internal_token)])
async def refund_payment(request: Request, body: _RefundIn, ...) -> dict:
findings.recommendation: Add a write-ahead auditor.record('whatsapp.payment_refunded', ...) naming reference_id + amount (never card data) before the refund call, and thread an idempotency_key through the refund the same way sends dedupe.
findings.fix: native-pay refund now write-ahead-audits whatsapp.payment_refunded (new critical auditable action naming reference_id+amount, never card data) BEFORE the money movement; idempotency is enforced by state (a completed refund leaves the payment not 'captured', so a replay is refused at PAYMENT_NOT_REFUNDABLE).

findings.title: Native-pay lookup and refund run blocking Graph I/O directly on the event loop
findings.scenario: adapter.get_payment_status() and adapter.refund() (MetaWhatsAppPayments) call get_json/post_json, which are synchronous urllib requests. Unlike every other Graph call in the service (register, media upload, status, messaging-limit all use asyncio.to_thread), these run inline on the single-worker event loop. One slow Meta payment call stalls EVERY other request in the pod, and refund makes two such calls (lookup + refund) back-to-back.
findings.evidence: lk = adapter.get_payment_status(configuration=body.payment_configuration, reference_id=body.reference_id)
findings.recommendation: Wrap get_payment_status() and refund() in await asyncio.to_thread(...) exactly as the register/status/media routes do.
findings.fix: get_payment_status (both routes) and refund now run via asyncio.to_thread, matching every other Graph call, so a slow Meta response no longer freezes the event loop.

findings.title: MARKETING WhatsApp templates are never forced into the consent map — they send with no consent check
findings.scenario: is_unmapped_marketing() (the guard that refuses an unmapped marketing template at write and boot) is only applied to the internal email/SMS Template upsert route. A WhatsApp template registered with category MARKETING (whatsapp_templates.CATEGORIES includes MARKETING) is never cross-checked against NOTIFY_CONSENT_PURPOSES. In notify(), consent is gated only when the template_key or event is present in that map, so a marketing WhatsApp campaign whose template name a developer forgot to map goes out under only the opt-out check (contract basis), with no lawful-basis check and indistinguishable in logs from a transactional send.
findings.evidence: return category == TEMPLATE_MARKETING and key not in (purposes or {})
findings.recommendation: Enforce the same unmapped-marketing refusal on WhatsApp template register/submit (registry.register when category==MARKETING and name not in NOTIFY_CONSENT_PURPOSES), and/or fail closed in _deliver_whatsapp when the resolved template category is MARKETING but no purpose maps.
findings.fix: WhatsAppTemplateRegistry.register now refuses a MARKETING template whose name is not in NOTIFY_CONSENT_PURPOSES (both the internal and v1 register routes pass the map), so a marketing WA template can no longer send with no consent check. Regression tests added.

findings.title: Internal catch-up reads return every tenant's inbound customer messages and recipients with no tenant filter
findings.scenario: GET /internal/whatsapp/inbound, /internal/notifications/receipts, and the coexistence echoes/history/contacts reads call changed_since()/*_since() with only a constant `kind` filter — no tenant scope. Any holder of X-Internal-Token (a single shared secret by default) can page the ENTIRE fleet's inbound customer message bodies, sender numbers, delivery recipients and template keys across all tenants. A single misconfigured or compromised peer service exfiltrates every shop's conversation content, defeating per-tenant isolation on the /internal tier.
findings.evidence: rows, cursor = await store.changed_since(after=after or None, limit=max(1, min(1000, limit)))
findings.recommendation: Accept a required tenant parameter on these catch-up reads and push it into the find() where-clause, OR gate them behind a distinct, narrowly-allow-listed caller in INTERNAL_ROUTE_POLICY_JSON so only the reconciliation consumer (not every peer) can read cross-tenant.
findings.fix: the catch-up reads (receipts, inbound, coexistence echoes/history/contacts) accept an optional tenant query param that scopes the store find() where-clause, so a per-tenant consumer cannot page the whole fleet's inbound customer messages through the shared internal token; fleet-wide default preserved for the reconciliation consumer, which the per-route internal caller policy already gates.

findings.title: BODY_LIMIT_BYTES (1 MiB) contradicts WHATSAPP_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES (16 MB) — media upload endpoints cannot accept their advertised size
findings.scenario: BodyLimitMiddleware rejects any request body over BODY_LIMIT_BYTES=1_048_576 with 413 before the handler runs. /internal/whatsapp/media/upload-handle and /upload-id take base64 bytes and validate up to WHATSAPP_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES=16*1024*1024, whose base64 form is ~21 MB. Any media upload above ~750 KB is rejected by the middleware with a generic PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, never reaching the handler's own 16 MB check — so carousel/header media of realistic size can never be uploaded, and the operator sees a confusing double limit.
findings.evidence: BODY_LIMIT_BYTES: int = 1_048_576  # 1 MiB   ... vs ...   WHATSAPP_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES: int = 16 * 1024 * 1024
findings.recommendation: Either raise the body limit for the media-upload routes (per-route limit), stream multipart instead of base64-in-JSON, or reconcile the two constants and document the true maximum a media upload can carry.

findings.title: Receipt monotonicity breaks on same-second out-of-order receipts (Meta timestamps are whole seconds)
findings.scenario: apply_receipt guards with `if ts >= d.receipt_ts`. Meta delivery/read receipt timestamps are second-resolution, so a `read` and a `delivered` for the same message frequently carry the SAME timestamp. If the `delivered` webhook arrives AFTER the `read` (Meta does not guarantee order), ts==receipt_ts satisfies `>=` and the delivery's receipt_status is overwritten from 'read' back to 'delivered' — the exact regression the comment above claims is prevented.
findings.evidence:
if ts >= d.receipt_ts:
            d.receipt_status, d.receipt_ts = receipt_status, ts
findings.recommendation: Rank receipt statuses (sent<delivered<read<failed as applicable) and only advance when the new status outranks the current one at equal timestamps, rather than relying on `ts >=` alone.

findings.title: apply_receipt does a non-atomic read-modify-write of the delivery row
findings.scenario: apply_receipt() reads the delivery via by_provider_message_id() then put()s the mutated copy. Two receipts for the same wamid processed concurrently (Meta batches + retries, multiple pods) both read the pre-update row and both write, so a later 'read' can be lost under a concurrently-written 'delivered'. No CAS/compare-and-set is used, unlike the idempotency reservation which correctly uses cas().
findings.recommendation: Use a CAS/optimistic-version update for the receipt fields, or make the receipt event log (which is already append-only) the source of truth and derive the delivery's latest receipt_status from it.

findings.title: Operator delivery log uses scan_all() (unordered) yet claims to return 'recent' attempts
findings.scenario: GET /api/v1/notifications/deliveries -> DeliveryStore.list() -> scan_all(_DELIVERIES, limit). scan_all returns the first N rows in the store's natural (insertion/arbitrary) order, NOT newest-first. As the deliveries collection grows, the operator's 'recent delivery attempts across the platform' screen actually shows the OLDEST rows and never the recent failures it exists to diagnose, and it is a whole-collection scan reachable from a request path.
findings.evidence: return await self._store.scan_all(_DELIVERIES, limit)
findings.recommendation: Replace with an indexed, sorted read (find with sort=('ts','desc')) the way whatsapp_outcome_counts and by_tenant already do; the whole-platform scan on a request path should be an ordered, bounded query.

findings.title: WhatsAppProvider port send() signature omits header_media_id/button_payload/url_button_param carried by every real adapter
findings.scenario: The Protocol declares send(to, template_name, language, variables, biz_opaque_callback_data, flow_token, flow_action_data) — seven params. FailoverWhatsApp, MetaWhatsApp and ConsoleWhatsApp all implement send() with three EXTRA positional params (header_media_id, button_payload, url_button_param) that the notifier passes positionally. Any new provider written to the documented port contract, or a runtime_checkable isinstance pass, is out of step; the notifier's positional call would break it.
findings.evidence: def send(self, to: str, template_name: str, language: str, variables: list[str], biz_opaque_callback_data: str = "", flow_token: str = "", flow_action_data: dict | None = None) -> str:
findings.recommendation: Update the WhatsAppProvider Protocol (and send_interactive/send_template_components as needed) to the full signature the adapters and FailoverWhatsApp actually implement, so the contract and the implementations cannot drift.

findings.title: meta.py returns a shared 'wamid:unparsed' sentinel that collides across sends and mis-attributes later receipts
findings.scenario: When Meta accepts a send but the body cannot be parsed, _post() returns the fixed string 'wamid:unparsed'. Two such sends both persist provider_message_id='wamid:unparsed'. A later receipt resolved via by_provider_message_id(wamid) does find(..., limit=1) and attributes the receipt to whichever of the colliding deliveries the store returns first — the receipt lands on the wrong message.
findings.evidence: return "wamid:unparsed"
findings.recommendation: Make the sentinel unique per send (e.g. 'wamid:unparsed:' + uuid4) so it stays truthy but never collides, or treat an unparseable accepted body as a failure with no id.

findings.title: Refund captured-amount guard is a two-call TOCTOU with no lock — concurrent refunds double-spend
findings.scenario: refund_payment() calls get_payment_status() ('captured' check) then refund() as two separate Graph calls. Two concurrent refund requests for the same reference_id both observe status='captured' and both proceed, issuing two refunds before Meta flips the status. The module's own comment admits 'per-tenant locking is layered in P6', so the once-only-by-state guarantee does not hold under concurrency today.
findings.evidence:
lk = adapter.get_payment_status(...)
    ...
    res = adapter.refund(reference_id=body.reference_id, ...)
findings.recommendation: Add an idempotency/lock keyed by (tenant, reference_id) around the lookup+refund pair (the same cas() reservation pattern the notifier uses) so a redelivered or concurrent refund is refused, not repeated.

findings.title: Raw-mode WhatsApp variable ordering sorts by key lexicographically, mis-ordering numbered params
findings.scenario: When no WhatsAppTemplateRegistry is wired (self._wa_templates is None), variables are ordered by `sorted(variables.items())`. Meta template body params are positional {{1}},{{2}},...; lexicographic key sort places '10' before '2', so a template with 10+ variables (or any non-zero-padded numeric keys) receives its parameters in the wrong order and renders incorrect content.
findings.evidence: ordered = [str(v) for _, v in sorted(variables.items())]
findings.recommendation: Sort numerically when keys are integer-like, or require the caller to pass an explicit ordered list in raw mode rather than inferring order from dict keys.

findings.title: drain()/_deliver misclassifies a queued whatsapp delivery as in-app
findings.scenario: _deliver() dispatches channel=='email' and 'sms', and everything ELSE (the else branch) to the in-app store. It is only saved today because _deliver_whatsapp never queues (finding notification-001). The moment WhatsApp failures are correctly routed to the queue, drain() will call _deliver('whatsapp', ...), fall into the else branch, and silently write the customer's message into the in-app feed instead of re-sending it via WhatsApp.
findings.evidence:
else:  # inapp — our own store, not a third party (whatsapp handled in _deliver_whatsapp)
                await self._inapp.add(InAppItem(...))
findings.recommendation: Make the else branch explicit for 'inapp' and raise/record 'unroutable channel' for anything unexpected, and give WhatsApp its own re-send path in drain() so fixing notification-001 does not silently divert messages.

findings.title: Inbound message content + contact PII is fanned onto the at-most-once bus even when conversation storage is disabled
findings.scenario: With WHATSAPP_CONVERSATION_STORE_ENABLED off (the default) nothing is stored, but _fan_out still publishes the full raw Meta message (customer text, media refs, contact profile) to whatsapp.message for any non-private (handover mode 'us') number. If a deployment flips WHATSAPP_DEFAULT_HANDOVER_MODE to 'us' or opts a number in, every inbound customer message body and contact PII is broadcast on a best-effort bus with no retention, redaction or minimization — a wider data footprint than the 'we store nothing' switch implies.
findings.evidence: await bus.publish(f"{_TOPIC}.message", Event(type=f"{_TOPIC}.message", payload={**base, "tenant": tenant, "message": msg}))
findings.recommendation: Publish a minimized envelope (ids, type, tenant, sender) on the bus and require consumers to fetch content from the durable, retention-bounded inbound log; keep raw content off the fan-out unless a deployment explicitly opts into content-on-bus.

findings.title: Internal embedded-signup twin has no rate limit while the operator route does
findings.scenario: POST /api/v1/notifications/operator/whatsapp/embedded-signup carries Depends(rate_limit); its internal twin POST /internal/whatsapp/embedded-signup does not. A caller holding the (default single, shared) X-Internal-Token can drive unbounded code-exchange attempts against Meta — burning Meta rate budget and enabling credential-spray — with no throttle, and the audit actor is empty ('') so attribution is weaker too.
findings.evidence:
@router.post("/whatsapp/embedded-signup", dependencies=[Depends(require_internal_token)])
async def internal_embedded_signup(request: Request, body: EmbeddedSignupInternalIn) -> dict:
findings.recommendation: Apply the same rate_limit dependency (and a real caller identity via INTERNAL_CALLER_DRIVER=static/jwks) to the internal onboarding, register, two-step-pin and refund routes that perform privileged Meta mutations.

findings.title: Tenant resolution failures on inbound webhooks are swallowed, silently mislabelling attribution
findings.scenario: Both _tenant_of() and the inline number_index.tenant_of() calls catch every exception and return "". A datastore hiccup on the number index means every inbound message and echo during that window is recorded and fanned out with tenant="" — attribution is lost with no counter, no WARN log, and no distinction from a genuine unbound number. A consumer then cannot tell whose message it is, and there is no signal that the index was down.
findings.evidence:
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a lookup miss must not stop the fan-out
                        tenant = ""
findings.recommendation: Emit a WARN/metric when tenant_of() raises (distinct from a legitimate miss) so a number-index outage is visible rather than looking like a flood of unattributable messages.

findings.title: Malformed internal-caller key maps are silently swallowed to {}
findings.scenario: _json_any_map() returns {} on any malformed/empty JSON. INTERNAL_CALLER_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON / INTERNAL_CALLER_JWKS_JSON feed this. A typo in the operator's JSON does not fail boot; instead the static/jwks driver silently sees zero keys, so every per-caller assertion fails verification and — with INTERNAL_CALLER_ALLOW_TOKEN_FALLBACK on (default) — everyone quietly degrades back to unnamed flat-token access, erasing the per-caller identity the deployment thought it enabled.
findings.evidence:
except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return {}
findings.recommendation: Validate these maps at boot (raise on malformed JSON when the matching driver is selected) rather than defaulting to an empty map that silently disables per-caller identity.

findings.title: Every WhatsApp send does three sequential preference reads
findings.scenario: _wa_recipient_allows() consults three keys (tenant-scoped, global, legacy raw-phone) with a separate await self._prefs.get(key) each, on the hot send path, for every business-initiated WhatsApp message and carousel. At campaign volume this triples the datastore reads per send purely for opt-out checking.
findings.recommendation: Batch the three reads (a single multi-get) or resolve them concurrently with asyncio.gather to keep the opt-out check to one round trip.

findings.title: Approved-template test-send bypasses opt-out and consent
findings.scenario: test_send_wa mode='template' resolves the provider straight from the pool and calls provider.send() directly, deliberately bypassing build_notifier — so it also bypasses the marketing opt-out check and the consent gate that notify() applies. An operator (or a stolen notifications.templates capability) can send an approved MARKETING template to any number that has opted out. It is capability-gated and audited (last-4 only), but the diagnostic can be used to reach unsubscribed customers.
findings.evidence: ok, _driver, mid = await asyncio.to_thread(provider.send, to, body.template_name, body.language, body.variables)
findings.recommendation: For template-mode test sends, still consult the recipient's WhatsApp opt-out (and refuse a MARKETING-category template to an opted-out number), so the diagnostic cannot become a compliance bypass.

findings.title: Internal /notify recipient has no format validation
findings.scenario: NotifyIn.recipient is only length-bounded (1..256). A malformed WhatsApp MSISDN or a bogus email flows through to the provider, where the error surfaces late (a wasted send, a Meta reject, a burned slot in the daily cap) rather than as a clean 422 at the door.
findings.evidence: recipient: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)
findings.recommendation: Add channel-aware recipient validation (E.164-ish for whatsapp/sms, RFC-lite for email) so a malformed address is rejected before a send is attempted.

findings.title: erasure audit uses subject_ref which raises on an empty PII_SALT outside production
findings.scenario: erase_subject() computes subject_ref(s.PII_SALT, ...) for the audit row. core.pii.subject_ref refuses an empty salt. The assert_pii_config_ok boot guard only runs in production, so in a staging/test deployment with an empty PII_SALT the first DSAR erase 500s instead of returning a clean error — the very late-failure the PII guard exists to prevent, just outside the environment it guards.
findings.evidence: ref = subject_ref(s.PII_SALT, body.tenant, body.subject)
findings.recommendation: Return a clear 503/precondition error when PII_SALT is unset on any environment that reaches this path, rather than letting subject_ref raise a 500.

findings.title: Operator email masking discloses the full domain and first local character
findings.scenario: _mask_recipient returns f"{local[:1]}***@{domain}" for emails, leaking the complete domain and first character. For a low-cardinality tenant (a company whose users are all @acme.sa) this plus the first initial substantially re-identifies the recipient from the cross-tenant delivery log.
findings.evidence: return f"{local[:1]}***@{domain}"
findings.recommendation: Mask part of the domain too (e.g. a***@a***.sa) or show only a hashed correlation token, since the log spans all tenants.

findings.title: No test exercises WhatsApp send-failure retry semantics or the _finish reservation-release paths
findings.scenario: The WhatsApp failure path (notification-001) records 'failed' and never queues, and the template-not-found/render-error paths leak the idempotency reservation (notification-002), yet both live in the most exercised module. These bugs survive because the test suite asserts happy-path send + email/SMS retry, but has no case for (a) a WhatsApp provider returning failure under NOTIFY_DELIVERY_MODE=queued, nor (b) a retried idempotency_key after a template-not-found. A test that recorded 'failed' would pass while measuring nothing about resilience.
findings.evidence: return await self._finish(idempotency_key, tenant or "", await self._on_failure(...))  # reached for email/sms only, never whatsapp
findings.recommendation: Add tests: a queued-mode WhatsApp send that fails must produce a QUEUED delivery with retry_at; and a same-idempotency-key retry after a template-not-found must send once the template exists (asserting the reservation was released).

findings.title: Graph base default is duplicated as a hardcoded constant in the adapters
findings.scenario: _DEFAULT_BASE='https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0' is hardcoded in whatsapp/meta.py AND whatsapp_payments/meta.py, duplicating WHATSAPP_GRAPH_BASE from config. If an operator bumps the Graph version via config but a construction path ever omits base_url (relies on the default), sends and payment lookups silently target a different API version than the rest of the service — a split-brain version that is invisible until Meta deprecates one.
findings.evidence: _DEFAULT_BASE = "https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0"
findings.recommendation: Have callers always pass the configured base and drop the in-adapter default (or assert it matches config at boot) so there is one source of truth for the Graph version.
